business_scope.primary_industry_name: Middle-Market Cross-Border Cross-Industry M&A Advisory Boutique

Agreement between the Government of the Arab Republic of Egypt and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (effective 1996)
Agreement between Egypt and Germany concerning the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force)

Convention between Egypt and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (signed 25 January 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended), together with its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 133 of 2003 and subsequent amending decrees), Unified Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Commercial Registry Law No. 11 of 1956, Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations, and Financial Regulatory Authority capital-market licensing and AML/CFT rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder, director, authorized manager, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or civil registry authority of the country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Origin-country notarization, origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then consular legalization by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Egyptian embassy in the country of issuance; Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so apostilles are not accepted

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or official company register extract of any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial registrar of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Official registry seal, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then Egyptian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or know-your-customer certificate confirming source of funds, business profile, and PEP status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the incorporation funds or the client relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-issued document, Arabic sworn translation by an accredited translator, and Egyptian consular legalization where the account is held outside Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Egyptian counsel or GAFI one-stop-shop representative for pre-incorporation filings and licensing procedures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the principal's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, Arabic translation, and Egyptian consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, and UBOs at onboarding and at each ownership change against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Egyptian Central Bank and Egyptian AML/CFT Unit blacklists. PEP status is collected by signed self-declaration and validated through commercial PEP databases, with enhanced due diligence automatically applied to foreign PEPs, family members, close associates, or any person connected with high-risk jurisdictions. Screening records and UBO files must be retained for at least five years after the termination of the client relationship or corporate interest.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop and Commercial Registry National Portal operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) at www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be rendered in Arabic in the memorandum of association and constitutes the sole statutory name. A Latin-character transliteration is permitted only for banking, contractual, and administrative convenience and must correspond phonetically to the Arabic name. Foreign-word names, including names of foreign parent companies, must be transliterated into Arabic script in accordance with the pronunciation and cannot employ words contrary to public order, state sovereignty, or Islamic or non-Islamic religious sensitivities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by written application filed with GAFI before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant must file a written appeal with the Chairman of GAFI's Legal Affairs and Alternative Dispute Resolution Department within 15 days of receipt of the rejection notice, attaching the official rejection form, the Arabic transliteration certificate, and a memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from existing registered names. GAFI must issue a decision on the appeal within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may institute administrative judicial proceedings before the Economic Court and may in parallel file a fresh application under a new Arabic transliteration to preserve the transaction timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the statutory registered address for a licensed M&A advisory boutique. The company must maintain physical premises in Egypt evidenced by a lease contract in its name, utility records, and an operational reception. A serviced office or business center may be accepted only if it provides a dedicated workspace, a physical reception area, one-year minimum occupancy, and unconditional access for service of process and inspection by GAFI, the Financial Regulatory Authority, and the Egyptian AML/CFT supervisor.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at 65% per annum for a Medium-Risk Enhanced M&A advisory LLC; the probability rises to approximately 85% if any UBO, source of funds, or success-fee payment relates to a FATF high-risk jurisdiction or a foreign PEP.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: AML Law filing requirement and compliance technology service subscription

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, Articles 24-51 (LLC provisions), together with the executive regulations and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 12-14 on investor services and one-stop incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Corporate Registration Directorate and One-Stop Shop, Commercial Registry Offices of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Contract (Aqd Al-Ta'sis), subscription schedule, managers' acceptance deeds and the incorporation application filed electronically through GAFI; formal issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Qayd)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory fixed minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC; the capital defined in the Company Contract must be fully subscribed and adequate to the corporate object. GAFI practice for a service boutique is a paid-up capital of at least EGP 50,000 (circa USD 1,600) deposited and held in escrow in a bank suspense account opened in the company's name pending issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founding members hereby subscribe to, and irrevocably accept, the full quota capital of the Company as stated in Article 3 of the Company Contract, and authorize the release of the escrowed subscription amounts to the Company's operating account upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. (2) The registered office situated at the address described in Article 5 of the Company Contract is adopted as the Company's statutory seat. (3) [Full Name_A], [Full Name_B], and [Full Name_C] are appointed as co-managers for a five-year term, with each authorized to sign individually for ordinary management acts, and jointly for real estate transfers, bank operations, and litigation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and investor account creation with GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investors Service Center and the GAFI e-Services portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an investor profile, conduct a company-name availability search against the commercial registry index, reserve the Arabic and English trade name, select the LLC form, and state the object as management consulting and M&A advisory; pay the reservation fee online and download the reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Investor profile registration form (electronic)
Passport or national ID copy of each founder
Legalized power of attorney if an agent files the application
Three proposed alternative trade names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar, resubmit with the alternative names; if the object wording is queried, align the object statement with ISIC 7020 and resubmit within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank capital verification and escrow deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking window of an Egyptian licensed bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt or Banque Misr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a suspense account titled 'LLC (name) - under formation'; deposit the subscribed quota capital from the founders' accounts; obtain a bank verification letter confirming the credited amount and its blocking pending incorporation; direct the bank to release funds upon GAFI issuance.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Draft Company Contract
Passport or national ID of each quota holder
Account application forms and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further proof on source of funds, file a detailed AML declaration and supporting bank statements; if the deposited amount is inconsistent with the contract, add a supplementary deposit or amend the capital statement and obtain a corrected verification letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Company Contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarization/Authentication Office of the Ministry of Justice coordinating with the GAFI legalization desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each quota holder or clearly authorized attorney must appear before the notary, verify identity, execute every page of the Company Contract, and pay the stamp duties; the notary authenticates signatures and returns multiple certified originals for GAFI and the bank.
required_dossiers: Bank capital verification letter
Draft Company Contract
Passport/national IDs of all quota holders and managers
Original power of attorney if representatives sign
Address and lease evidence for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies between contract capital and the bank letter, restate the capital schedule or obtain a supplementary bank letter and re-execute the contract on the same day; any typographical error can be corrected by initial sealing and re-authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation filing and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation at the GAFI one-stop shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) for company registration and the GAFI electronic incorporation platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Company Contract, subscription schedule, managers' acceptance deeds, and AML/KYC questionnaires; pay the official incorporation fees; the OSS verifies the reservation number, capital compliance, and office address, then issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a preliminary GAFI approval.
required_dossiers: Notarized Company Contract
Managers' acceptance deeds and their civil IDs
Bank capital verification letter
Lease contract for the registered office
Founder passports and AML/KYC source-of-funds forms
Proof of payment of official fees and e-stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the OSS issues a deficiency memo, respond with corrected documents within 15 working days; if approval is given subject to conditions, satisfy the conditions within 30 days or the preliminary certificate lapses and the process is reopened by a supplement letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registry entry and tax identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Central Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC with the Commercial Registry to obtain the Commercial Extract; then open the corporate tax file, secure the Tax Card, and register for e-invoicing and JIMID code; also register for VAT if applicable or apply for exemption from VAT on invoicing as per activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notarized Company Contract
Commercial Registry application and object classification
ETA registration forms, lease contract, and manager authority letter
Tax accountant authorization form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects due to object-code mismatch, submit a supplementary GAFI confirmation aligning the activity with ISIC 7020/NAICS 523150; if ETA issues late-filing penalties, file a rectification request confirming the notional start date and the immediate mitigation of the despatch records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating license, civil defense fire safety clearance, and environmental registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local district municipal licensing department, General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior), and the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) regional branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal operating license (Eijazat Tashgeel) for professional consultancy; submit floor plans, fire-safety readiness, and the Civil Defense inspection report; after clearance, receive the operating license. In parallel, register the low-risk office activity (Category C) with EEAA and file the self-monitoring declaration.
required_dossiers: Commercial Extract and Tax Card
Lease contract and authorized office floor plan
Civil Defense inspection report with evacuation routes
Fire extinguisher and alarm installation certificates
Electrical wiring and structural load safety certificates
EEAA low-risk environmental registration form (Category C)
Solid waste and e-waste handling declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality queries the activity class, present the GAFI object certificate and FRA classification note; if the Civil Defense refuses clearance, install additional alarm/extinguishing points and request re-inspection within 30 days; if EEAA re-classifies the office to Category B, file a simple Environmental Action Plan and obtain the registration amendment in 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial regulatory licensing and ancillary corporate governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) - Capital Market Licensing and Registration Administration; GAFI Annual Compliance Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the FRA financial advisory license under Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992 for M&A advisory services, evidencing the compliance manual, AML/CFT procedures, and professional indemnity arrangements; after issuance, file the annual governance statements, economic substance declarations, and ultimate beneficial ownership details with GAFI/FRA as required.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Extract and Tax Card
Company Contract and general assembly resolution
Compliance and AML/CFT manual
Principals' and compliance officer's CVs and clean criminal record certificates
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Municipal operating license and EEAA registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FRA queries the application, submit the requested clarifications within 10 business days; in case of refusal, lodge an internal administrative appeal and, if still denied, contest before the specialized economic court within 60 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investment Licensing Department, in coordination with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) for M&A advisory activities and the local Municipal Licensing Office for the operating permit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Operating License (Rokhasa Mahaliya) for consultancy services and FRA Financial Advisory Services License (Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992) for cross-border M&A advisory

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment - Governorate Branch Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Low Environmental Risk) - environmental registration only; no Full EIA report required under Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater discharged solely to the public municipal sewer system in compliance with Law No. 93 of 1962 regime (BOD <= 300 mg/L, COD <= 600 mg/L, TSS <= 350 mg/L); no production stack or VOC emissions from office activity; ambient air quality per Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000 with PM10 <= 150 µg/m3; noise within municipal business-district limits; office waste and e-waste handed to licensed municipal collectors or certified recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Clearance (Tarkhees Al-Himaya Al-Madaniyya) - certified fire extinguishers, smoke alarms, approved evacuation signage, and an annual civil defense inspection; structural load/occupancy safety certification for the leased office space; workplace clearance by the Ministry of Manpower under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 with occupational health inspection, first-aid kit, and social insurance registration of all staff; electrical safety certificate for office fit-out.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official e-portal: www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) by registering with the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) through the official e-portal or the competent regional tax office. Required documentation includes: certified copy of incorporation certificate, constitutional documents, local commercial registration extract, power of attorney issued to a local tax representative, certificate of the foreign entity's tax residence, proof of local fixed establishment/address, and valid identification of directors/shareholders. After document review, the ETA issues a combined Tax ID (TIN) covering corporate income tax, VAT, payroll, and stamp tax obligations. Non-resident service providers without a permanent establishment may instead be registered for withholding tax purposes and receive a dedicated non-resident TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a 'check-the-box' regime or domestic hybrid mismatch election mechanism. However, Egyptian Income Tax Law permits, upon ETA approval, consolidated tax returns for economically interdependent resident companies under specified conditions, though this does not alter the default entity-level taxation status of LLCs. Special economic zones (e.g., Suez Canal Economic Zone – SCZone) and investment-zone incentives may offer alternative tax treatments, but these are not entity classification elections; entities remain subject to the standard corporate income tax framework unless a specific investment agreement stipulates otherwise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 on Value Added Tax, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover threshold; mandatory VAT registration applies to any person making taxable supplies exceeding this amount. Importers of goods are required to register regardless of turnover level.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt enforces mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipts through the ETA's electronic invoicing portal. Taxpayers must integrate with the ETA-facing APIs and transmit each invoice/receipt in XML or JSON format in real-time; the ETA validates the submitted data and issues a unique transaction identifier (UUID) plus a QR code, after which the invoice is deemed fiscal and can be delivered to the buyer. The mandate covers all B2B and B2C invoices issued by registered taxpayers. Non-compliance triggers automated blocking of invoice issuance and statutory penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods may be zero-rated at 0% VAT once the goods are physically exported from Egypt and title has passed to a non-resident recipient. Supporting conditions: the export is documented through the official customs procedures; goods are shipped within the statutorily prescribed period from sales date; and for related-party transactions the price and economic substance satisfy transfer-pricing rules. Certain services supplied to non-residents for consumption outside Egypt, or services directly connected with export goods (such as handling, packing, shipping), may also qualify for zero-rating where specified by the VAT Law and explanatory guidelines.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form C & V) bearing customs seal
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT transfer confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Egyptian Tax Authority may retroactively claw back zero-rated VAT together with late-return interest and additional tax penalties under the VAT Law (penalties range between 50% and 100% of the undeclared tax due). In addition, fines of up to EGP 500,000 per ineligible invoice can be imposed, and fraudulent or fictitious export documentation triggers criminal prosecution under the Egyptian Penal Code and tax-fraud provisions, including imprisonment sanctions. The ETA also conducts post-clearance audits comparing customs export data, bank repatriation records, and VAT returns to detect abusive zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) / Egyptian Exchange Control Authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-float foreign-exchange regime. Current-account payments for licit cross-border advisory fees and operating expenses are generally convertible upon submission of a valid commercial invoice and CBE purpose code, while capital-account transfers including dividend/profit remittances, capital repatriation, and foreign investment exit require demonstrated historical source of funds, CBE approval for certain categories, and compliance with the Investment Law 72 of 2017, Law 194 of 2020 AML/CFT regulations and CBE FX circulars. Profit remittance is permitted after payment of taxes, statutory reserves, and audit; however, banks may request underlying transaction documentation, and residual hard-currency liquidity constraints can cause settlement delays. Foreign shareholders may maintain retained earnings in EGP or convert and remit at prevailing interbank rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE FX regulations, export receipts in foreign currency must be repatriated to an Egyptian licensed bank within 90 days from the date of shipment or performance of service (service fees, including advisory success fees, are treated as service export receipts). There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio after the 2016 liberalization; export proceeds may be kept in a foreign-currency account with an authorized bank or sold immediately to the interbank market. In practice, banks verify the underlying export/service contract, tax invoices, and customs documentation before crediting the account, and proceeds are required to be used for bona fide current or capital transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Qatar National Bank Al Ahli (QNB Al Ahli)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium with legal constraint: Foreign fintech EMIs are not permitted to open subsidiary accounts or pass-through rails in Egypt unless licensed or authorized by the CBE under Law 194/2020 and the CBE's payment systems and fintech regulations. Offshore e-money institutions may only connect through a licensed Egyptian bank or licensed electronic-payment processor; they cannot independently clear EGP transactions. Cross-border fee collection may use SWIFT via a corresponding Egyptian bank, but a digital EMI establishes only a money-transfer front, not a bank-account relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For first-time onboarding of a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC, CBE-compliant customer due diligence requires physical verification of at least one authorized signatory and all natural-person beneficial owners owning 25% or more. Directors may appear in person at the bank's office for an interview and certified document verification; remote opening is available only for limited non-resident deposit accounts or through the bank's approved digital onboarding with live video KYC, but pure remote opening is not a reliable statutory route for a cross-border M&A boutique because enhanced due diligence requires in-person verification for non-resident or higher-risk beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership or politically exposed persons in the corporate chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled corporate register, UBO register with percentage interests, org chart, passport copies, board resolution, proof of address, PEP status declaration and source-of-wealth evidence; where a PEP is identified, compliance escalation and enhanced monitoring program.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border success fees inconsistent with declared turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed advisory engagement agreements, transaction application and rationale, valuation of target, invoices and credit notes, bank statements showing margin fee flows, tax registration and VAT/GST filings, and detailed bank-commentary following CBE's transaction purpose code and AML questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership through offshore holding jurisdictions (e.g., BVI, Cayman)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chain-of-title ownership documentation, certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, audited financial statements, economic substance certificates, and explanation of treasury routing with supporting board approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers involving sanctioned or tax-constrained jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated OFAC/UN/EU/CBE sanctions screening report, transaction purpose and underlying contract, source of funds breakdown, counterparty beneficial ownership, and confirmation that national competent authorities have been notified if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injection must be effected via a licensed Egyptian bank through SWIFT MT103/MT202, with the wire referencing the CBE-approved purpose code (e.g., 'Foreign Direct Investment' / 'Capital Injection' under the General 7.1 codes). For foreign investors, capital must be transferred to the LLC's capital escrow account after issuance of the commercial registration and tax card; the bank will require the underlying shareholders resolution, certificate of incorporation, and e-signature records. Amounts are credited to the EGP operational account at the prevailing interbank rate or held in a foreign-currency subaccount for transaction traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for cross-border advisory settlement and trade disbursements may be executed by SWIFT MT103 cover / MT202 for correspondent routing; for merchant/LC-backed transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued under UCP600 may be used only where underlying goods are being acquired. For service fee payments and success fees, a standard SWIFT MT103 with clear invoice references, supporting documents, and the applicable CBE purpose code is the recognized clearing rail. Domestic settlement between dual-licensed banks clears via the RTGS system; EGP balances for cross-border invoices require conversion through the interbank market.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBE-approved plain-vanilla deliverable forward exchange contracts between an Egyptian licensed bank and the LLC for EGP/USD positions with tenors up to 12 months
FX swaps (deliverable, plain-vanilla or same-day roll) as bilateral contracts with a licensed bank for managing temporary currency gaps
Foreign-currency denominated account hedging via structured deposit or a covered foreign exchange transaction with CBE-compliant ISDA/PSA terms

Direct offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts concluded through the operating group's fully-owned foreign treasury subsidiary, subject to banking policy and restriction against the use of a foreign bank without a CBE license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (with audited financial statements annexed and UBO declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Income Tax Sector, electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; by 30 April for 31 December year-end entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of EGP 5,000-50,000 per Tax Procedures Law 80/2021 plus monthly delay addition at the CBE credit/discount rate + 2%; enforced collection and suspension of ETA services for continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and Ordinary General Assembly (OGM) approval record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' general assembly; Commercial Registry copy where publicity applies; audit report retained for ETA and EMLCU inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year entities); audited statements accompany the 30 April CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Dividend distribution and manager discharge barred without approved audited financial statements; OGM default exposes the LLC to judicial winding-up under Companies Law 159/1981

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Status Card (Tax Card) renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority - competent tax office for the legal person
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during Q1 (January-March) on the calendar-year cycle, alongside CIT return preparation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Card lapse blocks government contracting, tender participation, and municipal license renewal; re-issuance requires prior settlement of compliance penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation and client CDD refresh (AML/CFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal AML compliance officer (MLRO) under EMLCU supervision; GAFI one-stop-shop where beneficial-owner declarations are lodged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation as of 31 December completed by 31 March; additionally within 30 days of any quota transfer or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and imprisonment under AML Law 80/2002 (as amended) for incomplete or false UBO records; DNFBP registration revocation and enhanced ETA risk classification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry continuity confirmation and annual fee settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade) / GAFI investor services center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registration anniversary; corporate changes (registered office, managers, quota transfers) filed within 30 days of each event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for late data updates under Commercial Registry Law 34/1976; certified registry extracts withheld; repeated default permits the registry to flag the entity as inactive with strike-off risk

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit mandatory under Companies Law 159/1981 when LLC stated capital exceeds EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,000) or shareholders exceed 10; also mandatory for DNFBP M&A/corporate-finance advisory firms subject to AML regulation, for foreign-owned entities under GAFI supervision, and whenever any quota-holder validly requests an auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) per Ministerial Decree 110/2015 (and amendments), substantially converged with IFRS; financial-institution and listed-entity supplements per CBE and FRA requirements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quota transfers require notarized amendment and immediate update of the Register of Members; UBO data is confirmed annually as of 31 December, signed by the general manager and MLRO by 31 March, and reconciled with the ETA beneficial-owner declaration and GAFI records; new investors must evidence identity, source of funds, and nationality before admission
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share/quota ledger including transfer history)
Register of Directors/Managers and their authorities
Minute Book (general assembly and management resolutions)
UBO register maintained per AML Law 80/2002
Accounting records: journal, ledger, inventory register, and correspondence files per Commercial Law 17/1999

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential rate is available for ISIC 7020 M&A advisory services in Egypt. The effective burden remains 22.5% on tax-adjusted commercial profits after permitted deductions for staff costs, rent, professional subscriptions, depreciation, financing costs, and amortization of permitted intangibles. Free-zone investment incentives under Investment Law No. 72/2017 are ordinarily unavailable to an M&A advisory boutique and, if claimed, require exceptional SCA approval and real economic substance in the free zone.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 113 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) E-Tax portal at https://www.tax.gov.eg or via certified tax advisors; a Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form (TP-1) is attached to the same filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance corporate income tax payments are made on account by the end of the month following each calendar quarter.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within four months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year entity, the filing deadline is 30 April. Quarterly prepayments follow the same schedule. Foreign-company LLCs operating through an Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) are subject to the same deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of taxpayer, Egyptian Tax Identification Number (TIN), registered address, and ISIC business activity code 7020.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident LLC with an Egyptian PE must enter the Egyptian TIN and the registered Egyptian branch address. If no PE exists, the entity must not file this CIT return; income would instead be subject to source withholding by the Egyptian payer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period start and end dates covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must adopt the same fiscal year as the foreign LLC for annual CIT purposes unless ETA has approved a separate Egyptian accounting year. Closing date must be no later than the foreign entity's tax year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Return type tick-box: original return, supplementary or amended return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 'original' for the initial compliant filing. An amended return may be filed within five years from the statutory due date to correct disclosed mistakes before ETA assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenues and business receipts, including M&A retainers, advisory fees, success fees, and any consulting compensation paid on closing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Egyptian-source success fees must be declared regardless of the bank receiving the wire. Fees collected offshore in USD, EUR, or AED must be translated into EGP at the prevailing CBE exchange rate and included in gross income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses directly attributable to the business activity: legal due-diligence costs, transaction documentation costs, salaries, rent, travel and professional indemnity insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses wholly and exclusively incurred for the Egyptian PE are deductible. Home-office cost allocations are allowed only if supported by an arm's-length attribution analysis and retained TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after statutorily required add-backs and disallowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible management fees paid to related offshore service companies unless the recipient has real economic substance and the fee is at arm's length. Penalty interest, excessive entertainment, and political contributions are also add-backs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may carry forward only Egyptian PE losses, and only if the loss was duly declared in an original CIT return. The maximum carryforward period is five years. Foreign head-office losses cannot be set off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after net loss carryforward, subject to corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 22.5% corporate rate to the final positive figure. No treaty may reduce the domestic corporate tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory rate applied and any tax relief or tax credit claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only for direct Egyptian-source income taxed overseas and must be supported by a certified residency certificate and foreign return evidence. No separate treaty rate credit for corporate profits exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated CIT liability before advance payments and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must recalculate the liability using final audited figures. The quarterly prepayment credits are separately disclosed in Box 11.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance corporate tax payments, payroll tax credits, foreign tax credits, and any stamp duty credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident must attach a schedule reconciling all quarterly ETA debit receipts. Credits not used will create an estimated rebate or carryforward per ETA assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any resulting tax must be paid via the Egyptian banking system using the LLC's Egyptian tax account. A non-resident treasury team must never receive a tax refund without first presenting the beneficial ownership/tax card.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure: related parties, controlled transaction types, amounts, methodology, and comparability analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for an Egyptian LLC whose related-party transactions exceed the TP threshold. The non-resident parent and Egyptian PE must have consistent documentation; failure to file this schedule triggers automatic TP audit selection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return carries an administrative penalty of up to EGP 50,000 in addition to monthly default interest of 2% on the overdue tax; understatement caused by deliberate concealment adds an inaccurate-return penalty of 10% of the additional tax assessed and can lead to criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Law 91/2005 Articles 116–119.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to a non-resident corporate shareholder, unless a lower rate is available under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA). The withholding must be deposited with ETA before the dividend is remitted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a certified Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-state authority, complete an ETA treaty-relief application, and submit a beneficial ownership declaration proving the recipient is not a conduit. The application should be filed before the dividend distribution date, and ETA approval must be evidenced in the withholding account. If excess tax is withheld, the foreign shareholder may claim a refund through the Egyptian tax inspection office having jurisdiction, supported by the TRC, DTA article, bank credit advice, and withholding tax certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax is 20% on royalties and 20% on interest paid by Egyptian entities to non-residents. Most Egyptian DTAs reduce interest rates to 10–15% and royalties to 0–15% depending on the treaty partner and the type of intangible. For an M&A advisory boutique, any payment of branding, software license fees, or shareholder loan interest to a non-resident parent without a TRC and DTA approval will be over-withheld at 20% and create an absolute compliance burden.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared and maintained when the aggregate value of Egyptian controlled transactions with related parties exceeds EGP 10,000,000 in a fiscal year. Master File is required when the global group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds EGP 200,000,000 or the aggregate Egyptian controlled transactions exceed EGP 10,000,000. The disclosure form TP-1 must be attached to the annual CIT return whenever these thresholds are exceeded; ETA may also demand documentation within 30 days for lower-value transactions where a transfer-pricing accounting mismatch is evident.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted a generic Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute equivalent to GCC jurisdictions, but Egyptian tax law applies a strong substance-over-form doctrine, particularly under Article 87 of Law 91/2005. The ETA may disregard artificial contracts and corporate structures that lack genuine economic purpose, recharacterise revenue to the Egyptian entity that actually performs the M&A advisory work, and apply the beneficial-ownership limitation in tax treaties. A non-resident LLC maintaining an Egyptian advisory boutique must show institutional license, personnel, board control, physical premises, deal files, and transaction risk management in Egypt; otherwise treaty benefits are denied and the structure is assessed as a sham PE.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving closing success fees via SWIFT wire to an overseas bank account of the non-resident parent without issuing a valid tax invoice and without recording the fee in the Egyptian LLC's CIT return; intentionally omitting M&A completion fees from gross income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 116–119 of Law 91/2005, tax evaders risk imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000, plus assessment of the evaded tax with 2% monthly default interest. The ETA will also impose an inaccurate-return penalty of 10% of the additional assessed tax, and the underlying amount remains collectible through compulsory attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executive directors who knowingly route success fees to a related foreign entity without recognition are personally and jointly liable with the company for the unpaid tax, monthly interest, and penalties. Courts may pierce the corporate veil, impose a travel ban, and order civil restitution; conviction leads to disqualification from board membership and possible imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying unreasonably high management fees, success-fee shares, research fees, or shareholder loan interest to a related party in a low-tax jurisdiction; failing to prepare a Local File, Master File, or TP-1 disclosure; using an unexplained percentage split for cross-border M&A fees without a benchmarking study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may upwardly adjust the Egyptian taxable profit, disallow deductions for related-party payments, impose a TP penalty of up to 20% of the adjusted tax difference, and charge 2% monthly default interest. In egregious cases, the adjustment may be reclassified as tax evasion with criminal fines and imprisonment of responsible executives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve TP documentation knowing that the arm's-length pricing is false face personal civil liability for the entire tax deficiency plus penalties. The veil is pierced if the related remuneration is shown to have left the Egyptian entity without economic substance or commercial rationale; travel bans and director disqualification apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Egyptian LLC as an empty nominee with no real employees, no active Egyptian management, no M&A deal files, or no operational infrastructure; placing the entire advisory function offshore while booking invoices through the Egyptian entity solely to obtain treaty benefits or avoid PE exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 87 of Law 91/2005 and Egyptian Substance-over-Form case law, ETA will disregard the artificial arrangement, redistribute revenue to the actual function performed in Egypt, and deny deductions for payments made to shell unrelated or related providers. Administrative fines from EGP 50,000 up to EGP 200,000 may be imposed on the sham entity, and Commercial Registry authorities may order involuntary strike-off or winding up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly operate an Egyptian shell M&A boutique are personally liable for the taxes that the sham entity was created to avoid, as well as for insolvency costs if the entity was depleted by artificial payments. Travel bans, asset seizures, and personal criminal liability are available where the shell was used to defraud ETA or creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving large cross-border SWIFT success-fee payments from high-risk jurisdictions without carrying out robust customer due diligence, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the client, splitting invoices to evade threshold reporting, or failing to file a Suspicious Transaction Report with the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002, as amended, an entity found guilty of laundering proceeds can be fined up to EGP 5,000,000 and ordered to forfeit the laundered assets; senior managers may be imprisoned for a term of up to seven years, and the relevant regulatory licence or professional registration of the boutique can be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director or compliance officer who personally executes or conceals illicit fee transfers can be held criminally liable alongside the company, with imprisonment up to seven years, personal fines, confiscation of the director's property up to the laundered amount, and a travel ban pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profit dividends, paying offshore royalties, or paying shareholder interest without deducting statutory 10% divided or 20% interest/royalty WHT; failing to obtain and file the TRC before applying a DTA reduced rate; remitting profits directly from a foreign bank account to bypass Egyptian withholding controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian LLC as withholding agent is personally liable for the full uncollected withholding tax, plus monthly default interest at 2% and administrative fines proportionate to the under-withholding. ETA may issue an attachment order on all local bank accounts and enforce against the LLC's assets, and criminal tax concealment penalties can apply if the remittance was intentionally disguised.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for approving the dividend or repayment must ensure funds are reserved for WHT before any SWIFT remittance. Failure to do so exposes each relevant director to joint liability for the uncollected tax; courts may pierce the corporate veil and order civil personal remedies, travel bans against directors, and, in cases of fraudulent false declaration, imprisonment.
